vignette: Michael is a 58-year-old African man who works as a hairdresser in a small salon he runs with his wife, Sarah. Michael has always been passionate about his work and finds it both therapeutic and fulfilling to help clients look and feel their best. However, since a mugging two months ago, the joy he once derived from his occupation has been overshadowed by persistent anxiety and fear. The incident occurred late one evening as Michael was closing up the salon after a long day. He remembers feeling unusually tired but determined to finish quickly so he could head home to Sarah and watch a movie. As he locked the front door, he heard footsteps behind him. Before he could react, two masked individuals shoved him against the wall and demanded his wallet. Terrified, Michael handed over everything in his pockets without hesitation. The attackers took what they wanted and left, leaving Michael shaken but physically unharmed. He rushed home to Sarah, who immediately called the police. The trauma of the event has since lingered, affecting nearly every aspect of Michael's life. Since then, he has found it increasingly difficult to be alone or in dimly lit areas, especially at night. This has made closing up the salon a particularly stressful task for him. He now insists on finishing work earlier and leaves only when Sarah is around to accompany him home. Even during the day, Michael avoids venturing too far from his comfort zone within the community. Michael’s sleep has also been severely disrupted. He often wakes up in the middle of the night with a racing heart and drenched in sweat, reliving the moment he was confronted by the masked men. The nightmares are so vivid that they leave him feeling as though he is constantly on edge, expecting another attack at any moment. In his interactions with clients, Michael finds himself becoming easily startled by sudden movements or sounds, which sometimes leads to jolts and abrupt reactions. This has created a sense of tension in the salon that neither he nor Sarah can ignore. Clients have started noticing changes in Michael’s demeanor; he seems more irritable and less patient than before. Michael also reports flashbacks during his daily routines, where he momentarily re-experiences the fear and helplessness he felt during the mugging. These episodes are particularly intense when something triggers memories of that night—like the sound of footsteps or seeing someone in a hoodie, which resembles the clothing worn by one of the attackers. The mugging has also intensified Michael’s overall anxiety. He now frequently checks locks on doors and windows at home, even when he's sure they’re already secure. The constant vigilance makes him feel like he is always scanning his environment for potential threats. This hypervigilance extends to his interactions with customers; he often finds himself overly cautious around strangers, struggling to relax or fully engage in conversations. Despite these challenges, Michael remains committed to maintaining the salon and continuing his work. Sarah has been incredibly supportive, working alongside him to create a safer environment and trying to alleviate some of the pressures on Michael’s shoulders. However, as he continues to grapple with the lingering effects of the trauma, Michael finds himself questioning whether he will ever feel safe again. The incident has left a deep emotional scar that affects his daily life and work, leaving Michael in a state of ongoing distress as he tries to navigate through each day while managing the symptoms that persistently remind him of the mugging.
